source: Local time-class gate -- machine load, compiler and background processes move these numbers; NOT in CTest (AGENTS.md 4.4 rule 21: bench, not assertion). Run tools/check/check_perf_gates.ps1 to judge a build against this file.
note: The absolute lines come from SPEC.NF.PERF.02 (cat 10 MB >= 45 fps; full redraw <= 100 ms) and SPEC.FEAT.INTERACT.04 (first search over a 100,000-row scrollback <= 200 ms P95); the relative line (max_regression_percent) is those requirements' own 'regression > 10% is FAIL'. Metric keys are exactly those the bench writes under "metrics" in its --json= output. direction names the better side. A gate with relative=false is judged only by its absolute line. capture.build_config, capture.grid and capture.search_fixture all belong to the measurement contract: the gate FAILs on a sample whose optimization level, whose rows x columns, or whose search fixture differs from the capture, because a Debug build inflates the write chain by 20-30x, a different grid simply counts a different number of cells, and a fixture with a different row count, column count or match count scans a different amount of work (a table that reaches the 10,000-match cap stops early and reads as a speed-up) -- either way the reading no longer describes the same product.

capture.aggregation: median across runs -- the same rule the gate applies, so a reference and a reading are comparable
capture.build: msvc-bench preset (Ninja + MSVC, RelWithDebInfo), default config (dracula, Cascadia 14pt)
capture.supersedes: Three generations. (1) The first capture on 2026-10-02 ran the Debug default preset and reported cat 90.7 fps / scroll 7.15 ms / full redraw 12.5 ms / 0.68 MB/s. It did not record the optimization level, so numbers that looked like product cost were describing /Od /RTC1 code. (2) The first optimized capture that day (cat 736.828 fps / ingest 20.627 MB/s) predates G19, the framework-side single-width short-circuit inside aurora::unicode_cell_width; that primitive sits in the write chain, so the whole ladder moved together (chain 25.9 -> 41.1 MB/s). (3) This capture replaces the post-G19 one (cat 755.213 fps / scroll 1.262 ms / full redraw 1.220 ms / ingest 28.888 MB/s at grid 24x73): the framework now embeds and registers Cascadia Code under its own family name, so monospace_cell resolves the requested face instead of falling back through the default chain, the 14 pt cell went 13x26 -> 11x22 px, and the same 960x640 window now holds 28x86 cells (+37.4%). Frame time rose about 42% for that reason alone; the per-cell cost moved 0.720 -> 0.747 microseconds (+3.7%, inside the 10% window), which is why this is a contract change rather than a product regression. Superseded rather than rewritten in place: a benchmark reference has to say which build, which grid and which framework produced it.
capture.invocations: Three independent gate invocations of three bench processes each; each reference below is the median of that invocation's three medians

ungated.reason: Derivative of scroll_frame_ms_mean (1000 / mean); gating both would double-count one signal.
Count of measured frames, a sample-size diagnostic rather than a cost.
Derivative of cat_mb_per_s (bytes / wall); same signal counted twice.

Attribution rung: the producer chain alone (decode, parse, state machine, grid) with no session, no lock and no queue. Moving one rung usually moves its neighbours, so the product-facing rate is locked on cat_mb_per_s (B-7) instead. Only present with --write-side.

Attribution rung: the same corpus through Session (lock, dirty-row scan, damage queue) while the main thread drains the queue without painting; the gap to chain_mb_per_s is the session-side cost. Only present with --write-side.

The other statistic of the same 9 scans, and SPEC.FEAT.INTERACT.04 names only P95. Gating it too would lock a second line on one signal (scroll_fps and cat_wall_ms are excluded on the same rule). A systematic scan slowdown moves the whole distribution, so B-8 still sees it.

Sample size of the scan distribution, a diagnostic rather than a cost (same category as cat_frames). It is also what makes B-8's p95 coarse: summarize() picks index min(n-1, n*95/100), so with 9 samples the p95 IS the slowest scan of the process; the median across 3 processes is what stabilizes it.

gates.note: SPEC.NF.PERF.02's named metric: 10 MB fed through cat must hold >= 45 fps. Capture at grid 28x86: 543.231 / 543.117 / 534.657 across three invocations (1.6% span, adverse side 1.6%). The step down from the 24x73 reading is the cell count, not the product -- see capture.supersedes.

Three capture runs spanned 1.244-1.355 ms (8.8%): a 10% relative window would leave almost no room for background load, so only the requirement's absolute line judges it. A whole-screen paint regression also shows up in B-3 / B-5. The 28x86 re-capture reads 1.787 / 1.796 / 1.806 (1.1%), still only three invocations, so the line stays absolute-only rather than reopening on a low-jitter session.

One row dirty per frame: the cheapest view of the per-frame cost of dirty-row filtering, run splitting and colour resolution. Capture spread 1.2%; the 28x86 re-capture read 1.795 / 1.799 / 1.800 across three invocations (0.3% span). Per cell rather than per frame it is 0.747 microseconds against the 24x73 capture's 0.720 (+3.7%, inside the window), so the frame rose with the cell count and not with the cost of drawing one.
Tail of B-3; capture spread 2.7%, so the tail is worth locking. The 28x86 re-capture read 2.053 / 2.061 / 2.119 (3.2% span, adverse side 2.8%).

Frame cost while the 10 MB feed is in flight (whole-viewport dirty plus a concurrent producer thread). Capture spread 5.3%; the 28x86 re-capture read 1.841 / 1.841 / 1.870 (1.6% span, adverse side 1.6%).

Tail of B-5 with a wide capture spread (18.7% then, 9.4% on the post-G19 re-capture: 1.513-1.655) -- too wide for a 10% relative line. Judged instead against the requirement's own frame budget (1000 / 45 fps), so a periodic long frame that would drop under 45 fps reads red even while the mean looks healthy. The 28x86 re-capture reads 2.065 / 2.065 / 2.175 (5.3%), which is narrower but still one session's worth of samples, so the absolute-only rule stands.

Ingestion throughput. The first capture left it out on the belief that a write-side defect pinned it (gating a defect would freeze it in as the contract); that belief was a Debug-build artifact -- the optimized rate is 20.6 MB/s, and after G19 landed in the framework the post-capture rate is 28.9 MB/s. Raw single runs are NOT stable (a five-run probe spanned 19.2-21.3, 10.3%), which is exactly why the gate judges the median of three. The 28x86 re-capture reads 29.907 / 30.695 / 30.565, a 2.6% peak-to-peak span with 2.2% on the adverse side (a higher-is-better metric can only fail downward), so the 10% relative line has headroom. This number is not named by SPEC.NF.PERF.02: it catches write-side regressions that frame-time gates cannot see, since a slower producer simply yields fewer frames.

SPEC.FEAT.INTERACT.04: first search over a 100,000-row scrollback must answer in <= 200 ms (P95). The ruling (7.78 part 5) pins that sentence to the literal arm only -- the regex arm folds every row into UTF-16 for the engine and can read two orders of magnitude slower on a wide pattern, so that arm is guarded by the UI-side throttle 'rescan on Enter, never per keystroke' instead of by a time line here. Fixture per capture.search_fixture: 100,028 stored lines x 86 columns carrying 1,000 embedded matches, rare enough that the 10,000-match cap never triggers an early stop (a truncated scan measures less work and would read as a speed-up). Each process runs 9 cold scans with no warmup, because 'first' is itself the measured quantity; summarize() picks index min(n-1, n*95/100), so with 9 samples the p95 IS that process's slowest scan and the median across 3 processes is what stabilizes it. Capture readings (p95 per invocation): 33.499 / 34.237 / 32.533 (5.2% span, adverse side 2.2%), about 6x under the absolute line -- the scan is memory-bound on the grid walk, so the relative window is the tight one and it is affordable here. Pooling 9 cold scans was checked against a truly cold first scan rather than assumed: --search-runs=1 three times gave 32.093 / 33.197 / 31.351, within 2% of the 9-run mean and 4% below its p95, so the pooled p95 neither hides first-touch cost nor manufactures a ceiling. Same preset, window and default config as B-1..B-7; captured 2026-10-07 from the current bench binary, which emits the render metrics and this one from a single process, and the render gates re-pass against it.
